name: $clearCron
description: Clears an active cron, returns bool

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the cron

name: $setCron
description: Executes code on a cron expression

args.name: code
args.description: The code to execute

args.name: expression
args.description: The cron expression to run it on, such as 0 9 * * 1-5

args.name: name
args.description: The name for this cron

args.name: timezone
args.description: The zone to read the expression in, such as Europe/London

args.name: persist
args.description: Whether this cron is re-armed on startup, overriding cronConfig

args.name: maxOverdue
args.description: How stale a missed occurrence may be on startup before it is skipped

args.name: restoredTicksLimit
args.description: How many occurrences missed while down to replay on startup, overriding cronConfig

name: $clearTimers
description: Cancels and forgets every stored timer whose properties all match, returns how many

args.name: filters
args.description: Property and value pairs, all of which have to match

name: $findTimer
description: Returns every stored timer whose properties all match, as JSON

args.name: filters
args.description: property;value pairs, all of which have to match

name: $getAllTimers
description: Gets all existing timers from the database

args.name: kind
args.description: Only return timers of this kind

args.name: property
args.description: Return only this property of every timer, instead of all of them

args.name: separator
args.description: Join the properties with this, instead of listing them as JSON

name: $getTimer
description: Gets an existing timer from the database

args.name: kind
args.description: The kind of the timer to look for

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timer to get

args.name: property
args.description: The property of the timer to return

name: $timersCount
description: How many timers are stored, of one kind or of every kind, returns a number

args.name: kind
args.description: Only count timers of this kind

name: $wipeTimers
description: Cancels every stored timer and wipes them from the database

name: $eventData
description: Returns what an event carries besides its timer

args.name: property
args.description: The property to return, or every one of them as JSON

name: $newTimer
description: Retrieves a timer as the event left it

args.name: property
args.description: The property to pull

name: $oldTimer
description: Retrieves a timer as it was before the event changed it

args.name: property
args.description: The property to pull

name: $timerData
description: Returns what an event's timer was scheduled with

args.name: property
args.description: The property to return, or every one of them as JSON

name: $clearInterval
description: Clears an active interval, returns bool

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the interval

name: $setInterval
description: Executes code after given duration until canceled

args.name: code
args.description: The code to execute

args.name: time
args.description: How long to wait for before running this code

args.name: name
args.description: The name for this interval

args.name: persist
args.description: Whether this interval is re-armed on startup, overriding intervalConfig

args.name: maxOverdue
args.description: How stale a missed tick may be on startup before it is skipped, overriding intervalConfig

args.name: restoredTicksLimit
args.description: How many ticks missed while down to replay on startup, overriding intervalConfig

name: $clearTimeout
description: Clears an active timeout, returns bool

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timeout

name: $setTimeout
description: Executes code after given duration

args.name: code
args.description: The code to execute

args.name: time
args.description: How long to wait for before running this code

args.name: name
args.description: The name for this timeout

args.name: persist
args.description: Whether this timeout is re-armed on startup, overriding timeoutConfig

args.name: maxOverdue
args.description: How late this timeout may be on startup before it is discarded, overriding timeoutConfig

name: $clearTimer
description: Cancels a timer of any kind and forgets it, returns bool

args.name: kind
args.description: The kind of the timer to cancel

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timer to cancel

name: $executeTimer
description: Runs a stored timer's code now without touching the timer itself, returns bool

args.name: kind
args.description: The kind of the timer to run

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timer to run

name: $pauseTimer
description: Puts a stored timer on pause, returns bool

args.name: kind
args.description: The kind of the timer to pause

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timer to pause

name: $rescheduleTimer
description: Moves a stored timer's schedule without scheduling it from scratch, returns bool

args.name: kind
args.description: The kind of the timer to move, which is what the schedule below means

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timer to move

args.name: schedule
args.description: A delay for a timeout, a tick length for an interval, an expression for a cron

args.name: timezone
args.description: The zone to read a cron's new expression in. Left out keeps the one it had

name: $resumeTimer
description: Starts a paused timer again, from wherever its wait was left, returns bool

args.name: kind
args.description: The kind of the timer to resume

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timer to resume

name: $timerExists
description: Checks whether a timer is stored under this name, running or not, returns bool

args.name: kind
args.description: The kind of the timer to look for

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timer to look for

name: $timerRunning
description: Checks whether a timer is running right now, returns bool

args.name: kind
args.description: The kind of the timer to look for

args.name: name
args.description: The name of the timer to look for
